metadata.goal: Analyze how trip purpose relates to official destination land-use, departure time, distance, and transport mode across the supplied multiple-user trajectories.
metadata.category: Trip purpose, destination land-use, timing, distance, and mode
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 01 Purpose Destination Land Use
metadata.dataset_description: MTL Trajet 2016 mobility data with trip purpose, mode, timing, endpoints, trip metrics, and Montréal PUM 2050 destination land-use categories. User IDs distinguish participants, and the point tables provide speed profiles. The single-user case includes a repeated work corridor.
metadata.metric_note: `longest_stable_run_points` is the longest consecutive GPS-point segment whose adjacent speed changes stay within the mode-specific limit recorded in `stable_speed_change_threshold_kmh`: walking 0.15, cycling 0.25, public transit 0.40, and motor vehicle 0.60 km/h. This local continuity metric is distinct from full-trajectory `point_speed_std_kmh`.
metadata.source_note: Historical trajectories (2016) are spatially matched to the 2025 official PUM land-use taxonomy; do not interpret the categories as historical 2016 land-use observations.
metadata.land_use_reference: Archived PUM2050 Affectatio polygons (2025). Labels describe reference-map zoning at fixed endpoints, not surveyed activities at the time of travel.
metadata.motion_consistency_note: Point speed is the incoming segment GPS great-circle distance divided by elapsed time; the first point repeats the first outgoing segment speed. Earth radius: 6371.0088 km. Trip distance is the sum of these segment distances. avg_speed_kmh and mean_speed_kmh are total distance / elapsed time; avg_point_speed_kmh and point_speed_mean_kmh are unweighted means of the delivered point speeds. speed_cv is the population coefficient of variation of incoming segment speeds, excluding the duplicated first endpoint. trajectory_progress is point_index / (point_count - 1), not elapsed-time fraction. Timestamps and speed fields were reconstructed for internal consistency on 2026-10-09; GPS positions and insight wording were preserved. These are curated example records, not newly recovered observations.

insight_list.question: Which destination land-use types are represented across trip purposes, and how are health- and work-purpose trips distributed?
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
df = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
points = pd.read_csv(Path(dataset_path).with_name('trajectory_points.csv'))
print(pd.crosstab(df.purpose_group, df.destination_land_use))
insight_list.evidence: Official endpoint join: health has 22 Mixte and 18 diversified-activity destinations; work has 40 and 9, respectively.

insight_list.insight: Work- and education-related trajectories have clearly concentrated departure periods, whereas shopping, dining, and leisure trajectories are distributed across a broader set of departure times.

insight_list.question: How do distance distributions and transport-mode compositions differ among shopping, dining, health, and work trips?
insight_list.insight: Shopping and dining trips are generally shorter and less motor-vehicle-oriented than work trips.
insight_list.evidence: Shopping and dining trajectories are generally short, whereas health trips are longer and span a broader distance range; work trips have the widest distance distribution and are generally the longest. Walking, cycling, and public transit together account for most modes in the first three purposes; work trips use all mode categories, with motor vehicles the largest single group.
